description.p: Neoism is a hardware-accelerated terminal-first workspace for code, notes, agents, and multiplayer editing.
It includes a GPU terminal, Rust-owned IDE chrome around managed Neovim, file tree, buffer tabs, command palette, diagnostics, finder, and agent terminal tabs.

Key features:
Live CRDT collaborative editing
Agent-driven code changes with LSP integration
Markdown notes with vaults and graph views
Native Rust LSP, diff panels, and Warp-style UI
Stable Agent startup responsiveness, bounded transport, queue handoff, and scoped conversation-search improvements.
Stable background loading, fitting, blur, configuration, and first-frame window presentation improvements.
Stable search, queued compaction, presence, and provider-cache changes with production Agent GUI snapshot-contract alignment.
Stable conversation search, queued compaction, provider cache, Agent activity, and cross-platform presence improvements.
Stable conversation back-navigation and header improvements, with bounded Windows validation waits and pre-installer evidence checkpoints.
Stable MCP authorization/catalog improvements, connected subagent navigation, settings/modal refinements, and renderer ring effects.
Stable project conversations, unified navigation, tool composition, hosting and transport improvements, picker loading, and optional startup animation.
Nightly terminal-directory control, project selection, joined-document synchronization, and pointer/sidebar refinements.
Nightly project-grouped conversations, paginated navigation, unified directory picking, and shared desktop/web interaction improvements.
Nightly hosting eligibility, service startup, connection readiness, and server transport fixes with headless regression coverage.
Nightly hosting/startup fixes, Agent response-footer and composition presentation improvements, and connection lifecycle refinements.
Nightly tool-composition, server/invite workflows, and Git panel improvements. Stable releases remain on their separate update channel.
Improves Agent timeline stability, multiline composer scrolling, Anthropic reasoning and tool media, and browser-artifact integration.
Fixes Windows MSI major upgrades and adds readable service-and-tool timeline titles. Credits contributor Logan Settle.
Fixes Codex OAuth context limits using selected-account model maxima and effective input headroom, with consistent compaction budgeting.
Stable Agent, cloud workspace-worker, SDK, and rendering improvements. Preserves first-terminal directory following and excludes the experimental Servo runtime.
Stable workspace search and file-reading improvements, Agent scrolling refinements, and background and panel appearance updates. Experimental Servo runtime remains excluded.
Stable Agent UI, tool presentation, workspace search, and rendering improvements. Includes the first-terminal directory-following fix; experimental Servo runtime remains excluded.
Restores workspace and Explorer directory following when the first terminal changes directory. Servo runtime remains excluded.
Nightly Agent UI and frame-pacing improvements, live workspace search lifecycle fixes, streaming text reveal, and Codex usage inspection. Visible animations are preserved.
Fixes the Windows release-only Lua startup abort by preserving error unwinding, and adds release-executable Lua regression coverage.
YOLO stable release: fixes a Windows startup stack overflow during graphics adapter enumeration with an 8 MiB desktop main-thread stack reserve.
Substantial improvements to dev/release scripts, added AppStream metadata enhancements, better cross-platform support prep, and open-source readiness updates (MIT LICENSE, no Claude attribution).
